title: Plate tectonics and mountain building
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:51Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is written for Year 11 (lithosphere, convergent and divergent boundaries, magma, earthquakes and volcanoes), which is broader and at a clearly deeper level than this Year 8 point on plates pushing together to form mountains like the Himalayas.

draft.title: Plate tectonics and mountain building
card: The Earth's outer shell, called the crust, is broken into large pieces called plates. The plates move very slowly, by only a few centimetres a year.
Plates can push together, pull apart or slide past each other. The place where two plates meet is called a plate boundary.
Where two plates push together, rock at the edges is squeezed and forced upwards. Over millions of years this builds mountain ranges.
The Himalayas formed this way, where the Indian Plate pushes into the Eurasian Plate. They are still rising slowly today.
draft.remember: Mountains build up over a very long time where plates push together.

a.q: Which movement of two plates is most likely to build a mountain range?
opts: The plates push together and rock is forced up
The plates pull apart and rock is forced up
The plates slide past and rock is forced up
The plates stay still and rock is slowly worn down
a.why: When plates push together, the rock at their edges is squeezed and forced upwards. Pulling apart is the tempting option, but that movement does not squeeze rock, so it does not build mountains in the way the card describes.
a.clue: Think about what happens to rock when it is squeezed.

b.q: Scientists find that two plates in a region are slowly moving towards each other. What is most likely to happen there over millions of years?
opts: Rock at the plate edges is pushed up into mountains
The plates stop moving and the land stays the same
The crust is joined into one plate that is flat
Mountains sink as the plates press on them
b.why: Plates moving towards each other push together, which forces rock upwards and builds mountains over a very long time. The land does not stay the same, because the card says plates keep moving and the Himalayas are still rising.
b.clue: Remember what happens where plates push together.

a.best: The plates push together and rock is forced up

b.best: Rock at the plate edges is pushed up into mountains

check.summary: No problems found. Calling the plates the crust is a simplification, since plates also include part of the upper mantle, but it matches the chapter outline and suits Year 8.
